notes: t_87943990: the handoff audit enumerates the boot-key candidates with find(1) and reads their first 48 bytes with head(1), and the /verify page starts the audit before it reads its other sources, so the page answers in about 2 s instead of 6.8 s (the boot-key scan is 1.8 s of it). What the row proves is unchanged: same roots, same size window, same name exclusions, same first-48-bytes marker, same ssh-keygen check, and the Python walk remains the fallback when find cannot answer; WALK_TIMEOUT now bounds the read and kills the process group, and the dead _private_candidates helper is gone. Over 2026.11.21-2 (t_bf6092d7's gateway start-input cut): installer_sha256, audit_sha256, manifest.sha256, generated_at and this note move; the release manifest's audit row is re-derived from the installer the cut ships (tools/recut_release.py derives and checks it), so the signed document names the audit program a stranger runs. The served URL still serves 2026.11.19-5 until a deploy from a main that carries this cut.
